label: rem:golden-ratio-transport
title: Parallel transport of a golden-ratio parallelogram to $q_{\mathrm{gold}}$
html:
The golden ratio \varphi = (1+\sqrt{5})/2 appears twice in the Descartes elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q (golden ratio degeneration). It appears as a metric property (the conformal modulus of the elliptic fiber at q = q_0) and as an algebraic property (the root of the degeneration polynomial s^2 + s - 1 = 0 at q_{\mathrm{gold}} = 1/\varphi^2). Parallel transport along the q-connection (categorical q-connection) reveals these are the same \varphi, viewed from opposite ends of a geodesic in substrate parameter space.

Setup. The elliptic fiber \mathcal{E}_q at substrate parameter q is a complex torus \mathbb{C}/\Lambda(q). The period lattice \Lambda(q) is generated by 1 and \tau(q) \in \mathbb{H}. The modular parameter \tau(q) is fixed by the j-invariant j(q) = j(\tau). At q = q_0, we have j = 129.9 and real period \omega \approx 7.5565 (computation data).

Consider a parallelogram \Pi(q) in the period lattice with diagonal-to-side ratio \varphi. This fundamental domain encodes the conformal structure of the chiral fiber.

Schematic.

[Diagram]
LaTeX source
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9]
  % Π(q_0): a parallelogram with golden diagonal
  \draw[thick] (0,0) -- (2.0,0) -- (2.6,1.236) -- (0.6,1.236) -- cycle;
  \draw[dashed,->] (0,0) -- (2.6,1.236) node[midway,sloped,above]{$\varphi$};
  \node[below] at (1.0,0) {$\Pi(q_0)$: torus, diagonal $=\varphi$};
  % arrow
  \draw[->,thick] (3.4,0.6) -- (4.6,0.6) node[midway,above]{transport};
  \node at (4.0,0.2) {$q_0 \to q_{\mathrm{gold}}$};
  % node degeneration
  \draw[thick] (5.4,0) ellipse (1.0 and 0.6);
  \fill (6.4,0) circle (0.06);
  \node[below] at (5.4,-0.7) {$\Pi(q_{\mathrm{gold}})$: nodal $\mathbb{P}^1$};
  \node[right] at (6.4,0) {$\bullet$};
\end{tikzpicture}

The left panel shows \Pi(q_0) with a golden-ratio diagonal. The right panel shows its transport to q_{\mathrm{gold}} = 1/\varphi^2. Here one period diverges and the torus pinches to a nodal rational curve. The ratio \varphi acts as a length on the left and as the root of s^2 + s - 1 = 0 controlling degeneration on the right.

Transport equations. The q-connection \nabla_q = q^{-1}\nabla + (1 - q^{-1})(\iota_\xi\nabla) \varTheta_A depends continuously on q. As q decreases from q_0 to q_{\mathrm{gold}} \approx 0.382, the connection weight shifts:

q q^{-1} (spatial weight) 1 - q^{-1} (Reeb weight)
q_0 0.9011 +0.0989
1.000 1.000 0 (classical)
1/\varphi^2 \approx 0.382 \varphi^2 \approx 2.618 -\varphi \approx -1.618

Below q = 1, the Reeb term flips sign. It actively unwinds internal spin rather than accumulating it.

Degeneration. As q \to q_{\mathrm{gold}}, the j-invariant diverges, forcing \mathrm{Im}(\tau) \to \infty. The period lattice stretches without bound along one generator. The parallelogram degenerates:

  \Pi(q) \xrightarrow{q \to q_{\mathrm{gold}}}
   \text{infinite strip}
  \xrightarrow{ \text{pinch}}
   \text{node}.

The golden-ratio diagonal is destroyed as the torus collapses into a nodal rational curve.

The identity. The golden ratio transitions from a length ratio in \Pi(q_0) to the root of (s^2 + s - 1), which annihilates the Weierstrass coefficient r(q). The polynomial s^2 + s - 1 is the minimal polynomial of 1/\varphi over \mathbb{Q}. It appears in r(q) because Bring's surface is defined by \sum x_i = \sum x_i^2 = \sum x_i^3 = 0 in \mathbb{CP}^4. Its S_5 symmetry acts through fifth roots of unity \zeta = e^{2\pi i/5} satisfying \varphi = 2\cos(\pi/5).

The shape information of the parallelogram and the algebraic degeneration condition represent the same number. Parallel transport from q_0 to q_{\mathrm{gold}} transforms the geometric length into the algebraic instability threshold.

Reciprocal asymmetry. The inversion q \to 1/q maps z = \sqrt{q} - 1/\sqrt{q} to -z. At q_{\mathrm{gold}}, z = -1 and the chiral cubic factors as X(X^2+1) = 0. At q_{\mathrm{gold}}^{-1} = \varphi^2, z = +1 and the cubic X^3 + 2X^2 + 3X + 4 = 0 is irreducible. The fiber remains smooth with \Delta = -200 and j = 160. Bring's surface breaks the q \leftrightarrow 1/q symmetry. Although U_q(\mathfrak{g}) \cong U_{q^{-1}}(\mathfrak{g}), the elliptic curves \mathcal{E}_q \not\cong E_{1/q}.

Information transition. The parallelogram \Pi(q) is a fundamental domain containing exactly one period of chiral fiber information. Transporting it to q_{\mathrm{gold}} forces the information capacity of the fiber to diverge along one axis and collapse along the other. At the node, the distributed loop information concentrates at a singularity. The golden ratio marks the phase transition where chiral fiber information collapses from a distributed torus to a localized node.
